result:
The analysis is finished and PR #326 is marked ready. Of the issue's two stacked defects, only the first remains at master: the unimplemented BRDF mode. The "wedge not rasterised" defect is refuted from the test source.

**What the wedge is:**
- It is ordinary geometry: the front face of the first cube, with every vertex's w positive. It is not the negative-w wedge that #223 fixed.
- The test's vertex shader object contains no program, so the draw runs fixed-function. The model transform is applied after the view, so both cubes are rotated about the world origin and land off screen. The first cube just clips into the bottom-right corner; the second cube (the one with negative w) puts nothing on screen.
- A CPU model of the transform covers 610 of the golden's 614 wedge pixels and nothing outside it. The other 4 are pixels on the triangle's edge.
- That is also why "neither cube appears": both are drawn, off screen.

**Why ours shows the clear colour:** the suite blends by source alpha by default. With the BRDF stage producing 0 (alpha 0), a drawn pixel blends back to exactly (18,18,18,254). So the issue's proposed check at pixel (639,479) reads the same whether or not the triangle is drawn, and cannot tell the two cases apart.

Today the zero doesn't even come from the placeholder in the BRDF case. `stage_consistent` treats the stage as disabled because its feeding stages aren't dot-product stages. `get_sampler_type()` also has no BRDF case, so the stage-2 sampler is never declared.

**The BRDF rule, fitted per pixel against the three goldens:** the 3D lookup is (s, t, r) = (θ_eye, θ_light, φ_light − φ_eye, wrapped). The eye/light textures store θ in the high 16 bits and φ in the low 16 bits, sampled nearest.

| axis | exact | within 1 texel |
|---|---|---|
| s = θ_eye | 99.8% | 100% |
| t = θ_light | 100% | 100% |
| r = φ_light − φ_eye | 99.3% | 100% |

All three goldens are identical because the test's "blank" option clears only one of the six cube faces, and the wedge samples none from it. It doesn't mean the lookup ignores its inputs.

**Price (offline):** 605 of 610 modelled pixels match exactly. Each of `BRDF_e0_l0`, `BRDF_e0_l1` and `BRDF_e1_l0` should drop from 614 differing pixels to about 9. If the eye/light textures were sampled filtered instead of nearest, only 187 would match.

**Code:** the change is `docs/lanes/brdf315/brdf315-psh.diff`, which applies cleanly to master. It adds a BRDF case to `get_sampler_type()` returning a 3D sampler, stops requiring dot-product feeding stages, and emits the lookup. `glsl/psh.c` is held by lane.wbufdepth24 (#266), so I did not commit it; it needs that lane or a grant. It has not been compiled, so the holder's build will be its first.

**Loose ends:**
- **No prediction registered.** The test arm needs the `psh.c` change on my branch, so it can't exist here. The arm is written out ready to register in NOTES §5, including what to expect at pixel (639,479).
- **The read the brief asked for is still queued** (`1790373098-brdf315-964945`, Texture BRDF at fab230935e). No capture on disk was taken at a ref containing #223. The `0-a-now-8e683b3a26` sweep has been idle at suite 024 of about 71 for 20+ minutes. By the blend argument the read can only return (18,18,18,254), so it confirms rather than decides, and NOTES says so.

Preflight passed with `--allow-tracker`; CI on the last push hadn't reported when I stopped. The PR's `Files:` line matches the diff (four files under `docs/lanes/brdf315/`), and the report is posted on #315.
